OCTOBER FIELD LOG — CAT HEAD AREA, LAKE MARION

This is a retrospective of our firsthand October fishing trips, not a claim that the same fish are holding there today. October's fishing gave us a documented starting point for evaluating the seasonal move into November.

OCTOBER 5 — Our trip produced approximately 240 pounds of catfish, including four fish over 50 pounds. Wind was reported around 7 mph from the north-northeast to north-northwest. These are trip totals, not a lakewide catch forecast.

OCTOBER 13 — Fishing near Cat Head, morning surface water temperature was about 75.7°F. Bait was observed in approximately 10–18 feet of water. The recorded catch included a 6-pound channel catfish and an 8-pound blue catfish, followed by a blue reported around 40 pounds later in the trip.

OCTOBER 21 — Near Cat Head, water temperature ranged from approximately 70.3°F to 72.8°F during the trip. We caught blue catfish weighing approximately 30 and 25 pounds in about 18 feet of water, and later a blue around 40 pounds in approximately 22 feet on an upslope.

WHAT THE LOG TELLS US — During the documented October outings, productive water included bait-related structure and depth changes in the upper-teen to low-20-foot range. The October 21 upslope catch shows why the relationship between contours can matter as much as any single depth. These results document where and how we fished on those dates; they do not establish a current bite at Cat Head or across Lake Marion.

NEXT STEP — November coverage will investigate a new location and compare its contours, bait, water conditions, sonar observations and actual fishing results against this October baseline. Public reports explain the general-area structure and reasoning; exact GPS positions and advanced tactics are available to Master Fisherman Patreon supporters.

DIVERSION CANAL FLOW OUTLOOK — November 4, 2026

LIKELY DIRECTION: Lake Marion toward Lake Moultrie. This is an informed hydraulic interpretation, NOT a measured Diversion Canal discharge or current-speed reading.

LATEST PUBLISHED DAILY LEVELS (November 2): Lake Marion 74.22 ft; Lake Moultrie 74.13 ft. Marion stood approximately 0.09 ft (1.1 inches) higher. These figures are dated daily readings, not simultaneous real-time measurements. A higher Marion pool supports the potential for eastward movement through the connecting canal; the elevation difference alone cannot determine flow in cubic feet per second or current speed.

HYDRO OPERATIONS: Santee Cooper's schedule available November 4 shows Jefferies Hydro tentatively discharging from midnight to 8 p.m. and St. Stephen Hydro not scheduled to run. Jefferies draws from Lake Moultrie and releases to the Cooper River; this can help sustain the Marion-to-Moultrie elevation gradient. St. Stephen discharges from Lake Moultrie through the Rediversion Canal toward the Santee River. Its lack of scheduled generation does not mean the Diversion Canal is motionless.

FISHING INTERPRETATION: Some Marion-to-Moultrie water movement is plausible under these conditions, but do not promise a strong bite-producing current or a specific canal velocity. Local wind, changes in generation and lake elevations can change conditions. Treat this as a directional outlook and verify onsite before relying on current for boat handling or fishing presentation.

OFFICIAL SOURCES: Santee Cooper lake data and tentative hydro schedule: https://azapp-lakespublic-prd-001.azurewebsites.net/ ; explanation of Diversion Canal control: https://www.santeecooper.com/community/lakes/lake-data/ . Updated November 4, 2026. Replace this dated interpretation when newer readings or operating schedules are published.
